# Bubbles Quality Gates Catalog

## Goal
Resolve "what is gate G0XX" and "which script enforces this" without re-reading the entire governance corpus. Use this as the entry point into the gate catalog.

## When to use
- A guard (state-transition, artifact-lint, regression-quality, regression-baseline, etc.) failed with a `G0XX` label
- Designing a scope's DoD and need to know which gates apply
- Writing a test and need to know which gate IDs the test should cover
- Auditing whether a scope's DoD covers all gates relevant to the change

## v4.1.0 gate refinements

Gates G073, G090, G022, G041, G040, G008A, G009, G056 received non-breaking refinements in v4.1.0. See [`docs/v4.1.0-delivered-pending-activation.md`](../../docs/v4.1.0-delivered-pending-activation.md) for the per-gate behavior change and how scopes opt in via `Scope-Kind:`, `Lockdown-FRs:`, `deliverableFiles[]`, `phaseStubs{}`, and report.md anchor references.

| G095 | Discovered-issue disposition — every observed issue is FILED immediately on discovery (bug artifact + spec/scope/DoD status flip), never merely reported to the user, "recommended" for a future workflow, or deferred | `discovered-issue-disposition-guard.sh` |
| G097 | Requirement-mechanism correspondence (named mechanism ↔ code, warn-and-justify) | `requirement-mechanism-guard.sh` |
| G098 | Observability posture declared (wired/opted-out; undeclared WARN, project-flippable to block; fake-wired / opted-out-malformed / unsupported-schema fail loud; framework source EXEMPT) | `observability-posture-guard.sh` |
| G099 | Observability opt-out freshness (recorded + expiring opt-out; missing required optOut field fails loud; expired revisitAfter = non-blocking route-required reminder) | `observability-opt-out-guard.sh` |
| G100 | Observability SLO evidence (BLOCKING when posture: wired + an instrumented scope's `observabilityWorkflow` targets a workflow with an `slo:` link; captured `.specify/runtime/observability/<workflow>.slo.json` must MEET the `traceContracts.observability.slos` target; a contract-declared metric absent from `observed` is a breach; malformed / wrong-workflow evidence fails loud before numeric compare; missing jq/yq fails CLOSED; framework source EXEMPT). Division of labor: G026 ensures the stress/load test EXISTS + cites the SLO registry; G100 ensures the captured evidence MEETS the target. | `observability-slo-guard.sh` |
| G101 | Release-delivery reconciliation — every `delivery=required` feature in `docs/releases/<phase>/features.md` (machine-bound via `<!-- bubbles:feature id=… spec=… delivery=required -->` + a `bubbles:reconciled-packet` header) MUST map to a TERMINAL + VALIDATE-certified spec; promised-but-unspecced / non-terminal / blocked / implement-self-certified required feature = finding; WARN-grandfathered without the header, BLOCKING with header or `--require-coverage` (goal/sprint release-phase convergence); malformed reconciled packet fails loud; framework source EXEMPT; compile-time twin enforces `rootOutcome.targetReleasePacket` coverage in `scenario-compile-lint.sh` | `release-delivery-reconciliation-guard.sh` |
| G110–G126 | Release-train + upkeep + propagation + incident + framework gates: release-train discipline, flag-default-off-on-other-trains, backup / restore-drill / BCDR evidence, env-pollution isolation (G115), offsite-backup-required, audit-trail immutability, backup-retention / PII-classification / secret-rotation declared, propagation policy / validation / ledger, incident severity declared, framework-health evidence, model-tier floor | `release-train-guard.sh`, `env-pollution-scan.sh`, `propagation-policy-guard.sh`, `model-tier-advisory.sh` + targeted guards |
| G127 | Capability-consumer freshness (framework-source self-validation: every `state: shipped` capability in `bubbles/capability-ledger.yaml` declares a non-empty `consumers:` list whose every path exists on disk; blank-only list = ORPHAN, stray blank entry = MALFORMED, missing path = DANGLING; partial/proposed/deprecated exempt; repos with no ledger no-op; missing yq fails CLOSED only when a ledger is present; the G029 integration-completeness standard applied to the framework's own ledger) | `capability-consumer-freshness.sh` |
| G128 | Session-cap enforcement (aggregate whole-session sibling of G082): mechanically enforces the `sessionBudget` caps `maxTotalConvergenceIterations` / `maxWallClockMinutes` / `maxToolCalls` recorded in `.specify/memory/bubbles.session.json`; DEFAULT-OFF (all caps null → no-op), enforced only when a cap is set AND its aggregate is measurable; RFC3339 wall-clock via jq `fromdateiso8601` (GNU/BSD-identical); state-transition Check 40; no `--skip`/`--force`/`--ignore` bypass; a breach emits a `blocked` envelope with finding G128 and stops the session | `session-cap-guard.sh` |
| G129 | `repository_binding_classification_discovery_conformance_gate` (BLOCKING): rejects ambient repository inference by requiring one actionable same-session repository before local state, scoped discovery, commands, or dispatch; authority is explicit repository/target > durable same-session boundary > sole eligible repo, while unbound multi-root requests refuse; enforces `TARGETLESS_MODE`, `resolvedRepositoryRoot/specs`, exact session/root/decision/revision provenance from one immutable packet capture, scoped goal nodes, public redaction, and upstream-first ownership with no bypass | `repository-binding.sh`, `repository-binding-conformance-guard.sh` |
| G130 | `domain_invariant_correspondence_gate` — ADVISORY-UNTIL-CONFIGURED (the domain-invariant sibling of G097); INERT unless a repo declares an optional `domainModel:` block in `.github/bubbles-project.yaml` (a repo with no block — including the Bubbles source repo — is a clean no-op). Where G097 asks "a requirement names PKCE/OAuth2/HMAC — does the code implement it?", G130 asks "a `domainModel` business invariant (e.g. `Order.status ∈ {created,paid,shipped,refunded}`) — is it mechanically ANCHORED or just prose?". Each `domainModel.invariants` entry clears via ANY of: (a) an `enforcedBy` mechanism token in the scope's declared implementation files (`.sql` migrations included), (b) an adversarial `provedBy` test that rejects the violating input, or (c) an explicit `## Domain-Invariant Justifications` / `Invariant-Justification:` disclosure — honest disclosure over mechanical green. Specs whose `state.json.createdAt` is absent or earlier than 2026-07-27 are WARN-grandfathered. No `--skip`/`--force`/`--ignore` bypass. | `domain-invariant-guard.sh` (state-transition delegated tail Check 41) |
| G131 | `domain_model_consistency_gate` — ADVISORY-UNTIL-CONFIGURED consistency NUDGE (the DOM-SST sibling of G130); INERT without the optional `domainModel:` block (a repo with no block — including the Bubbles source repo — is a clean no-op). Where G130 asks whether a declared invariant is anchored, G131 asks the coherence question: does a feature keep its domain declarations IN SYNC with the shared SST? It nudges when (1) a feature's `design.md ## Data Model` declares an entity absent from the shared `domainModel.entities` — promote it up; or (2) an Outcome-Contract `INV-*` id is absent from `domainModel.invariants` — declare it in the shared model so G130 can check it. ADVISORY BY DEFAULT (prints findings, exits 0); blocks ONLY when a repo sets `domainModelConsistencyGuard: block` (the same shape as the G072 opt-in). FEEDS G044 a structured model for the cross-spec regression sweep. No `--skip`/`--force`/`--ignore` bypass. | `domain-model-consistency.sh` (delegated tail Check 42) |
| G132 | `reference_existence_gate` — ADVISORY-UNTIL-OPT-IN phantom-reference detector; the mechanical half of the No Phantom References rule in `agents/bubbles_shared/claim-grounding.md`. Resolves relative markdown link targets against the linking file's directory and reports every target that exists as neither file nor directory. DIVISION OF LABOR: G021 verifies a claimed COMMAND ran, G072 tags HOW evidence supports its claim, `gate-id-grep.sh` resolves GATE ID references — none verify a cited PATH exists. Deliberately skips external schemes, absolute paths, bare `#anchor` links, placeholder targets containing `< > { } $ *`, fenced code blocks, inline code spans, and bare backticked paths (a `.github/bubbles/...` path is often a downstream projection). Caller-supplied scan surface with NO default (the `macos-portability-guard.sh` precedent). Inline exemption `ref-ok:<reason>`; no `--skip`/`--force`/allowlist bypass. Advisory by default (prints, exits 0); blocks ONLY when a repo sets `referenceExistenceGuard: block` (the same shape as the G072 opt-in). LIMIT: catches dead paths, not a live path whose content fails to support the claim. | `reference-existence-lint.sh` |
| G133 | `collected_test_count_gate` — BLOCKING; refuses test evidence whose own output states that ZERO tests ran. Closes the gap the ≥10-line raw-output rule left open: a downstream e2e suite collected no tests for 15 days while twelve spec commits recorded passing-looking evidence, because the runner exited non-zero (which reads as ordinary test failure) and raw output from a broken runner is still raw output. The missing assertion was never "is there output" but "did any test actually run". Scans ONLY text inside fenced code blocks — the fence is what separates captured runner output from prose. Inside a fence, an explicit collection-zero signal from jest, playwright, pytest, go, cargo, vitest, mocha or `node --test` is a finding. The pattern set is deliberately small because generic patterns drown the signal (bare `0 total` matched jest's `Snapshots: 0 total` 354 times; bare `0 passed` matched the tail of `10 passed`). Evidence with no recognisable count is REPORTED, not failed. RATCHET: pre-existing hits are frozen in a per-repo `<repo>/.specify/collected-test-count-guard.baseline` generated with `--update-baseline`; it may shrink, never grow. No `--skip`/`--force`/`--ignore` bypass. | `collected-test-count-guard.sh` |

| G134 | `goal_fidelity_gate` — BLOCKING; makes the IMP-038 goal-fidelity capabilities load-bearing. `goal-contract.sh` can freeze/verify a goal, `work-boundary-resolve.sh` can refuse an undeclared boundary, and the envelope validator can refuse dishonest finding accounting — but none is REACHED unless a runner calls it, so a run that simply never called them passed everything. Checks the six boundaries where drift enters, each independently selectable: `pre-planning` (contract exists, schema-valid, FROZEN — an unfrozen contract can be edited afterwards to match whatever the run did — and names a repository); `post-planning` (spec.md has a non-empty Outcome Contract, state.json declares a `workBoundary`, `execution.goalContractRef` points at the SAME goal the session holds); `pre-dispatch` (candidate repo/spec/path resolve in-boundary under strict mode, supplied `goalRef` carries the current digest); `post-finding` (no changed path fell outside the declared boundary — handling a finding never authorizes editing outside the approved reach, the specific way a bounded run turns unbounded); `post-compaction` (resumed `goalRef` still matches, so a resume cannot silently continue against a superseded revision); `pre-certification` (report.md references the declared Success Signal, Hard Constraints were stated, spec is not certifying against an already-superseded revision). Also carries the G070 repair for ordinary feature work. Exits 0 / 1 (boundary failed) / 2 (usage). No `--force`/`--skip`/`--ignore` — an unsatisfiable boundary is NARROWED, or expanded via `goal-contract.sh revise --approval-note` with recorded operator approval. 39-case hermetic selftest, each case pairing a green fixture with its drifted variant. | `goal-fidelity-guard.sh` |
| G135 | `autonomy_posture_gate` — BLOCKING; keeps the IMP-039 autonomy posture surface internally consistent. The spec shipped a resolvable dial, a corrected enum, an opt-in `unattended`, a never-suppressible floor, a decision ledger and posture persistence — but AUT-2 was precisely a declaration describing behavior the implementation did not have, and nothing stopped that recurring. Checks the four places drift enters: (1) the never-suppressible floor still exists AND still enumerates its six items, so it cannot be hollowed out behind a surviving heading; (2) the `autonomy` enum in workflows.yaml and the resolver's `VALID_AUTONOMY` agree exactly in BOTH directions — declared-but-unimplemented is the AUT-2 shape, implemented-but-undeclared is undocumented behavior; (3) `unattended` with an unbounded session budget is still refused with exit 3 AND still names `E039-UNATTENDED-UNBOUNDED` (an unnamed refusal is not actionable), while a bounded budget still resolves, so the rule cannot be satisfied by refusing everything; (4) the resolver still refuses every bypass flag. Exits 0 / 1 (findings) / 2 (usage). No `--force`/`--skip`/`--ignore` — a posture that cannot satisfy the floor is CHANGED, never exempted. 15-case hermetic selftest, each pairing the green fixture with a drifted variant. | `autonomy-posture-guard.sh` |
| G136 | `human_acceptance_terminal_gate` — BLOCKING; refuses a terminal transition while any acceptance item in `uservalidation.md` is still unchecked. The hole is narrow and was load-bearing: `artifact-lint.sh` requires at least ONE checked `[x]` and never rejects an unchecked one, so one checked plus five unchecked passes lint and the spec reaches a terminal status with five behaviors no human accepted. Lint is the WRONG place to repair it — lint also runs during PLANNING, where a checked-by-default template is legitimate (it records what WILL be accepted, not that a human already ran it), so tightening lint would either break planning or force it to fabricate acceptance up front. The terminal transition is where the claim stops being provisional. Runs ONLY when the resolved target status is `done`; a ceiling-bound mode is not claiming human acceptance and an open checklist is correct for it. Parses only the `## Checklist` section using the SAME awk reader `artifact-lint.sh` uses, so the two cannot silently desync, and a `[ ]` under `## Notes` is ignored. THE GUARD NEVER EDITS THE FILE — checking a box on the author's behalf would fabricate exactly the acceptance the gate requires. No `--force`/`--skip`/`--ignore`. Two selftest cases: the BUG-029 shape itself, and its adversarial partner proving the section parser does not over-reach. | `guards/tail-delegated-gates.sh` (Check 43) |

| G137 | `release_ladder_schema_gate` — BLOCKING for a repo that DECLARES a release ladder; AUTO-EXEMPT otherwise. Sibling of G101, deliberately separate: G101 asks "is every promised required feature delivered?", G137 asks the prior question "is the ladder itself well-formed, ordered, and stably identified?" A repo can be structurally clean and honestly red, or delivered and unprovable; collapsing them would let either failure mask the other. The PRODUCT declares its ladder (`<!-- bubbles:release-ladder schemaVersion=1 phases=a,b,c -->` in `docs/releases/README.md`), headers, `dependsOn`, and bindings; the FRAMEWORK enforces only internal consistency and NEVER invents a ladder — no declaration means EXEMPT, since inventing one for a repo without a release ladder would be a false finding. Checks: one packet header per phase; `schemaVersion` refused not best-effort parsed; header phase equals its directory; `dependsOn` equals the full transitive predecessor set in ladder order; `id`/`spec`/`delivery` mandatory; closed `delivery` vocabulary; `deferred-to` resolving to a known LATER phase (never itself, never backward — a backward defer is an unreachable promise); `assurance` only on required bindings; `carried` declaring its regression posture; one capability id binding one spec across every phase. Fail-loud on a declaration naming no phases, a duplicated phase, or an unsupported `schemaVersion`. No `--skip`/`--force`/`--ignore`; `--ladder` cannot relax anything. 17 selftest cases: 1 control, 13 adversarial. | `bubbles/scripts/release-ladder-schema-guard.sh` |
| G138 | `release_packet_completeness_gate` — BLOCKING for a repo that ships `docs/releases/`; AUTO-EXEMPT otherwise. Enforces the "no fewer" half of the release-packet contract. `bubbles.releases` states "Exactly 8 docs per phase, no more and no fewer", but only "no more" was mechanical — `release-packet-location-guard.sh` rejected a non-canonical doc inside a packet while nothing asserted the canonical eight were present. |
| G139 | `action_risk_classification_integrity_gate` — BLOCKING; requires every classified CLI action to carry a risk class the gate can actually interpret. `pre-tool-risk-gate.sh` is a live PreToolUse hook that decides ALLOW/WARN/BLOCK before an action runs, so its verdict is only as trustworthy as the class it reads. The lint now validates every registered command, every `overrides:` value, and CLI/registry parity in both directions; an unrecognized class fails closed to `block`. |
| G140 | `phase_name_enum_integrity_gate` — BLOCKING; constrains every phase name a packet or an agent definition may write to the phases `bubbles/workflows.yaml` actually registers — the adjacent agent-id column was already enum-constrained while phase stayed free text. Covers `currentPhase`, `phase`, `executionHistory[].phasesExecuted[]` and `execution.completedPhaseClaims[]`, plus `currentPhase` authored in agent definitions. Ratcheted via a per-repo baseline that can only shrink; no flag or env var suppresses a finding. |

## Canonical Test Taxonomy (binding)
| Category | Means | Real-stack? | Mocks permitted? |
|----------|-------|-------------|------------------|
| `unit` | Isolated logic, fast | No | Yes (internal) |
| `functional` | Real-dep functions, may touch DB/filesystem | Optional | External only |
| `integration` | Multi-component, real deps, real test DB | **Yes** | **External only** |
| `ui-unit` | Component tests with mocked backend | No | Yes (backend) |
| `e2e-api` | API workflow vs live stack | **Yes** | **External only** |
| `e2e-ui` | UI workflow vs live stack | **Yes** | **External only** |
| `stress` | Burst load vs live stack | **Yes** | **External only** |
| `load` | Sustained load vs live stack | **Yes** | **External only** |

A test that uses `page.route()`, `context.route()`, `cy.intercept()`, `msw`, `nock`, `wiremock`, or any internal-service mock and claims to be `integration` / `e2e-api` / `e2e-ui` is misclassified. Reclassify it as `ui-unit` (or `unit`) and write a real live-stack test to fill the gap. The framework treats this misclassification as blocking.

## Adversarial regression for bug fixes
Bug-fix regression tests MUST include at least one adversarial test case — input that would FAIL if the bug were reintroduced. Tautological regressions (all fixtures already satisfy the broken code path) do not count. Enforced by `regression-quality-guard.sh --bugfix`.

## Resolving a gate failure
1. Note the gate ID printed by the guard.
2. Open the enforcing script in `bubbles/scripts/` and read the failing check's prose.
3. Fix the underlying gap (in the spec, scope, evidence, test, or code).
4. Re-run the guard. Do not change the test/assertion to silence the failure.

- `agents/bubbles_shared/quality-gates.md` — full gate catalog with rationale
- `agents/bubbles_shared/state-gates.md` — state-claim integrity gates
- `agents/bubbles_shared/claim-grounding.md` — the No Phantom References rule G132 enforces
- `agents/bubbles_shared/test-fidelity.md` — live-stack authenticity
- `agents/bubbles_shared/e2e-regression.md` — persistent regression expectations
- `bubbles/workflows.yaml` — gate-to-mode wiring
- `bubbles/scripts/gate-id-grep.sh` — surface every gate ID referenced in the repo
